stdout:
[0] Electrical energy is convenient to transmit, distribute and convert.
Wires can carry it to distant places, where it can be distributed to different users.
Suitable devices can convert electrical energy into mechanical energy, internal energy, light and other forms.
[1] A transformer can change the voltage and current of alternating electricity over a wide range.
An ideal transformer does not lose energy, but a real transformer does.
Changing voltage and current is important in many electrical and radio devices, as well as in long-distance power transmission.

[2] Devices that supply electrical energy convert other forms of energy into electrical energy.
Examples include batteries, electrostatic generators, thermopiles① and the solar cells used on spacecraft.
A fuel cell can convert the chemical energy released by a reaction between hydrogen and oxygen into electrical energy.
A magnetohydrodynamic generator uses hot ionized gas, or plasma, flowing through a magnetic field to convert energy of the gas into electrical energy.

[3] ① A thermopile uses the electromotive force produced when junctions made from different materials are at different temperatures.
    break: {"before":"Devices that supply electrical energy convert other forms of energy into electrical energy.\nExamples include batteries, electrostatic generators, thermopiles① and the solar cells used on spacecraft.\nA fuel cell can convert the chemical energy released by a reaction between hydrogen and oxygen into electrical energy.\nA magnetohydrodynamic generator uses hot ionized gas, or plasma, flowing through a magnetic field to convert energy of the gas into electrical energy.","after":"① A thermopile uses the electromotive force produced when junctions made from different materials are at different temperatures."}
[4] The characteristics of each device determine where it is useful.
An electrostatic generator can produce a large potential difference, but it supplies only a small current.
A battery bank can supply a larger current, but its operating time is limited by conditions such as the energy stored in it.
    break: {"before":"① A thermopile uses the electromotive force produced when junctions made from different materials are at different temperatures.","after":"The characteristics of each device determine where it is useful.\nAn electrostatic generator can produce a large potential difference, but it supplies only a small current.\nA battery bank can supply a larger current, but its operating time is limited by conditions such as the energy stored in it."}
[5] An **electromechanical induction AC generator** converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction.
Its basic principle and structure are relatively simple, and a suitable design can produce the required voltage and supply a large current to a load.

[6] In the rest of this chapter, the term “generator” refers to an electromechanical induction AC generator.
